findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Note that removing the analyzers coercion row orphans the `_as_str_dict` import in _config_schema.py (its only caller) and plan to drop that import (and consider whether _config_coercion._as_str_dict itself becomes dead).

findings.finding: Deleting the analyzers coercion row at _config_schema.py:716 orphans the `_as_str_dict` import at _config_schema.py:32 — it has no other use site — which `make lint` will flag as an unused import; the plan does not mention this cleanup.
scenarios: After removing the coercion row, the `_as_str_dict` import in _config_schema.py becomes unused and `make lint` (AC5) fails
findings.suggested_fix: Add removal of the `_as_str_dict` import from _config_schema.py:32 to the edit set; evaluate whether _config_coercion._as_str_dict has any remaining caller and remove it too if not.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the AC3 proving procedure explicitly: capture `rebar metrics` output to a baseline file before deletion, then `diff` against post-deletion output and assert empty.
evidence: 'rebar metrics produces byte-identical output before and after on this repo'
No command shown to capture the pre-removal baseline or to diff it against the post-removal output
findings.finding: AC3 asserts 'byte-identical output before and after' but names no concrete capture-and-diff procedure, leaving the before-state capture implicit.
scenarios: Executor forgets to snapshot output before starting the removal and cannot prove byte-identity afterward.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC3: 'Capture `rebar metrics > /tmp/before.txt` before the change; after the change `rebar metrics > /tmp/after.txt && diff /tmp/before.txt /tmp/after.txt` produces no output.'
